focus: Q4: How safe is upgrading or re-pinning a copied Skilled tree, and what would make re-pin, the overlay-guard hook and rollback safer or easier to recover from?
answeredQuestions: Q4: How safe is upgrading or re-pinning a copied Skilled tree, and what would make re-pin, the overlay-guard hook and rollback safer or easier to recover from?

graphEvents.label: Q4 re-pin, guard and rollback safety
Rollback restores without comparing the current tree
Guard fails open when the engine cannot judge
Stage plan skips regenerate and verify
Shell writes bypass the guard; one engine spawn per path
Re-pin runs are never listed or pruned
Guard runtime coverage is absent from overlay docs

label: Rollback restores every backed-up path without hashing the current destination, so a manual repair made after a failed re-pin is silently overwritten; the plan shows the backup contents, not a diff.
The overlay guard fails open on every judgement error, so a partial upgrade that removes or breaks overlay-engine.cjs leaves overlay-owned writes unguarded exactly when the tree is damaged.
A stage re-pin blanks regenerate and verifyGenerated, so a green stage plan can be followed by a live failure after the backup.
The guard does not parse shell writes, and it spawns the engine once per path with a 3-second timeout, so multi-path patches are slow and a timed-out path is allowed.
Every live re-pin writes a backup run folder, success included, but no command lists or prunes runs and only the failure path prints the run id.
OpenCode has no guard adapter and /doctor:overlay never mentions the guard, so runtime coverage and kill switches are invisible to an external-repo user.

direction: Replace the hash-verified file backup with a git-based restore for rollback
reason: writeBackup already includes the manifest, state, layout links and regenerate outputs, and verifies every byte before and after a restore; a git restore would not cover uncommitted overlay state and would require a clean worktree.
